Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the GlobalTech Solutions Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to GlobalTech Solutions’ earnings call. With me today are John Thompson, CEO; Susan Davis, CFO; Michael Lee, COO; and David Chen, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our press release and earnings slides, which are available on our IR website. Please note that this call may contain forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to John Thompson.

John Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Emily, and welcome, everyone.

We had a solid quarter with performance driven by several key initiatives. First, I’d like to discuss our sales guidance, forecast, and trends by segment for the next quarter and a preliminary view for the full year. While we anticipate navigating some headwinds in specific segments, particularly related to inventory corrections and market softness in consumer-centric areas, our diversified portfolio and strategic focus on high-growth markets like Automotive and Industrial IoT are expected to provide resilience and drive overall growth. Our midterm strategy remains centered on innovating next-generation analog and mixed-signal technologies, which will be key to capturing future market share. Looking specifically at Smart Mobile Devices, we expect inventory levels of our components to remain elevated throughout Q3. The slower-than-anticipated demand growth is attributable to several factors: increased competition in the mid-tier smartphone market, extended replacement cycles for existing devices, and a general consumer pullback on discretionary spending related to macro-economic uncertainties. We are projecting a 15% decrease in revenue for this segment in Q3 2023 compared to Q3 2022, landing at approximately $750 million, down from $882 million. This reflects both the reduced demand and a more aggressive pricing environment to manage the existing inventory. The slowdown is most pronounced in the Asia-Pacific region, particularly in China, where local manufacturers are gaining market share and consumer confidence remains subdued. North American and European markets are showing slightly better resilience, but still below previous forecasts. To mitigate this, we are actively working with our key mobile device partners to optimize their component usage and explore new product designs that incorporate our latest technologies. Additionally, we are implementing a targeted promotional campaign in emerging markets to stimulate demand. We are also accelerating our R&D efforts to develop more power-efficient and feature-rich components for next-generation 5G devices, anticipating a rebound in demand in late 2023 or early 2024. On the other hand, our Home and Industrial IoT segment is expected to demonstrate strong performance, largely mitigating the impact of the inventory correction in the broader IoT market. The increasing customer demand for our advanced analog and mixed-signal technologies in both the Home and Industrial sectors is a key driver. We forecast a 20% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, up from $1.91 billion. This growth is primarily driven by the industrial sector, where demand for our sensor technologies and connectivity solutions remains robust. Our investment in advanced sensors and connectivity solutions tailored for industrial automation and smart home applications is paying off. For example, our new line of low-power, high-accuracy pressure sensors is gaining significant traction in the industrial robotics sector. We are also seeing strong adoption of our secure, low-latency connectivity solutions for smart home devices. We are strategically partnering with leading industrial automation companies to integrate our technologies into their next-generation platforms. This collaborative approach allows us to gain early access to market trends and tailor our solutions to meet specific customer needs. While the more consumer-centric portions of the IoT market are experiencing some softness, we are focused on the higher-margin, more resilient segments within the industrial space. Our Automotive business remains firmly on track to deliver approximately $1 billion in revenue for the full year 2023. This represents a significant milestone and validates our strategic focus on this high-growth market. We anticipate consistent growth in Q3, driven by strong demand for our powertrain, safety, and infotainment solutions. We expect Q3 revenue to be approximately $260 million, a 30% increase compared to Q3 2022 ($200 million). The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) is fueling demand for our automotive-grade components. Our investments in silicon carbide (SiC) power devices are particularly paying off, as these components are critical for improving the efficiency and performance of EVs. We are actively pursuing new design wins with leading automotive manufacturers for next-generation EV platforms. Our goal is to become a leading supplier of critical components for the automotive industry, leveraging our expertise in analog and mixed-signal technologies. For Communications Infrastructure and Data Center, we expect to see a decline in revenues for this end market throughout the second half of 2023. The slowdown is primarily driven by a moderation in capital expenditure by major telecommunications companies and data center operators, following a period of significant investment in 5G infrastructure and cloud computing capacity. We are forecasting a 10% decline in revenue for this segment in Q3 2023 compared to Q2 2023, reaching approximately $450 million. We anticipate this trend to continue into Q4. While the overall market is softening, we are focused on maintaining our market share in key areas, such as high-performance optical transceivers and power management solutions. We are also actively exploring opportunities in emerging areas, such as edge computing and private 5G networks, which are expected to drive future growth in this segment. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing more energy-efficient and cost-effective solutions for these emerging applications. Finally, we expect our Personal Computing end market to remain at approximately 3% of total 2023 revenue. This reflects our strategic decision to de-emphasize our presence in the personal computing market and focus on higher-growth, higher-margin segments. We anticipate stable revenue performance in Q3, in line with previous quarters. Revenue is expected to be around $75 million. While we are not actively investing in this segment, we will continue to support our existing customers and maintain a presence in select niches where we have a competitive advantage.

We also made meaningful progress with our net margin and diluted EPS results. This adjusted EPS of $0.53 represents a 12% increase compared to the $0.47 we reported in the same quarter last year (Q3 2022). This strong performance is particularly noteworthy considering the challenging macroeconomic environment, characterized by persistent inflationary pressures and fluctuating consumer spending patterns. While some of our competitors have reported declining profitability, our strategic initiatives and operational efficiencies have allowed us to not only maintain but actually improve our bottom line. Our net margin for Q3 2023 came in at 8.7%, a 0.8 percentage point improvement from the 7.9% we recorded in Q3 2022. This improvement can be attributed to several key factors. We saw a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. This growth provided significant operating leverage, allowing us to spread our fixed costs over a larger revenue base. The revenue surge was fueled by a successful product launch in the North American market, specifically our new line of sustainable packaging. We've successfully negotiated more favorable terms with our key suppliers, resulting in a 3% reduction in our cost of goods sold (COGS) as a percentage of revenue. Our strategic decision to diversify our supplier base and invest in more resilient supply chain technologies, like our predictive inventory management system powered by AI, has proven invaluable. We previously experienced significant disruptions due to reliance on a single supplier in Southeast Asia, but that risk has been mitigated. While we continued to invest in strategic growth initiatives, particularly in our R&D department focused on next-generation materials, we were able to manage our Selling, General, and Administrative (SG&A) expenses effectively. SG&A increased by 10% year-over-year, but this was less than the 15% increase in revenue, resulting in a lower SG&A to revenue ratio. A major driver of SG&A efficiency was the successful implementation of our cloud-based ERP system, which streamlined our administrative processes and reduced redundant tasks. We expect further benefits from this system in future quarters. While we were not immune to inflationary pressures, our pricing strategies and cost-saving initiatives helped us to offset the negative impact. We implemented selective price increases across certain product lines, while also focusing on value engineering to reduce material costs without compromising product quality. Our consumer research indicated that customers were willing to pay a slight premium for our commitment to sustainability, providing additional pricing flexibility. The adjusted diluted EPS of $0.53 reflects the improved net margin and revenue growth discussed above. However, it's important to note a few nuances. Our ongoing share repurchase program contributed marginally to the EPS growth. We repurchased 5 million shares during the quarter at an average price of $35 per share, reducing the number of outstanding shares and thereby increasing EPS. The board authorized an additional $200 million for share repurchases, signaling our confidence in the company's future prospects. Our effective tax rate for Q3 was 22%, slightly higher than the 21% we recorded in Q3 2022. This increase was primarily due to changes in the geographical mix of our profits. Unfavorable currency exchange rates, particularly the weakening of the Euro against the US dollar, had a minor negative impact on our reported EPS. However, our hedging strategies partially mitigated this impact. North America and Europe performed exceptionally well, driven by the successful launch of our eco-friendly packaging line. Asia-Pacific, while still growing, experienced slower growth due to ongoing COVID-related restrictions in certain regions. We are closely monitoring the situation in Asia-Pacific and are prepared to adjust our strategies as needed. We expect to see some recovery in the region in the coming quarters as restrictions ease. The implementation of our new AI-powered demand forecasting system has enabled us to optimize production schedules and minimize inventory costs. This system has contributed significantly to our operational efficiency and profitability. Looking ahead, we are cautiously optimistic about the remainder of the year. While the macroeconomic environment remains uncertain, we believe that our strategic initiatives and operational efficiencies will enable us to continue to deliver strong financial results. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue growth of 12-14% and adjusted EPS of $2.10 - $2.20. Our focus on sustainability is resonating with consumers and providing a competitive advantage. Investments in technology are driving operational efficiencies and improving our bottom line. Diversification of our supplier base has made our supply chain more resilient. Geographic diversification is crucial for mitigating risk and capturing growth opportunities.

On a broader level, our Customer Long-Term Agreements (LTAs) and Supply Agreements continue to provide valuable visibility into pricing dynamics. As previously reported, our strategic shift towards securing LTAs with key customers has yielded substantial benefits in enhancing pricing visibility. Before the widespread adoption of LTAs, fluctuating spot market prices created uncertainty and negatively impacted profitability. Now, with approximately 65% of our revenue in Q3 2024 secured under LTAs (up from 58% in Q2 2024), we have greater confidence in predicting revenue streams and managing cost fluctuations. Specifically, the LTAs have allowed us to predict revenue with greater accuracy. Our revenue forecast accuracy has improved by 8% year-over-year due to the locked-in pricing and volume commitments within the LTAs. This improved accuracy allows for better resource allocation and investment planning. For example, Q3 revenue came in at $2.25 billion, only 1% off our forecast, a significant improvement compared to the 4% variance we saw in Q3 2023. The LTAs have also allowed us to negotiate better supply agreement terms. The guaranteed demand provided by LTAs has strengthened our position when negotiating supply agreements. In Q3, we were able to secure a 3-year supply agreement with a key raw material supplier, locking in a 5% price reduction per unit compared to previous spot market purchases. This translates to an estimated cost savings of $15 million annually. We've also been able to implement dynamic pricing strategies. While LTAs lock in baseline pricing, they also allow for dynamic pricing adjustments based on market conditions. We've successfully implemented clauses that allow for price adjustments linked to specific commodity indices (e.g., the Platts index for certain energy-intensive materials). This has enabled us to capitalize on favorable market movements while still providing customers with price certainty. LTAs have fostered deeper partnerships with our key customers. The collaborative nature of these agreements allows for open communication and proactive problem-solving. For example, we worked with a major automotive client in North America to adjust delivery schedules under their LTA, mitigating potential production disruptions caused by a temporary parts shortage at their end. Sectors that saw the most LTA adoption, such as the industrial manufacturing sector in North America, experienced a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year, contributing $800 million of the total Q3 revenue. This growth is directly attributable to the volume commitments and stable pricing provided by the LTAs. Despite the overall positive impact of LTAs, underutilization charges are emerging as a significant area of concern. These charges arise when customers fail to meet the minimum volume commitments outlined in their LTAs. Total underutilization charges for Q3 2024 amounted to $35 million, representing a 20% increase compared to $28 million in Q2 2024. This upward trend warrants immediate attention. The majority of underutilization charges originate from the EMEA region, accounting for 60% of the total. This is primarily driven by macroeconomic headwinds in Europe, including high energy prices and supply chain disruptions, which have impacted our customers' production levels. The Asia-Pacific region accounts for 25% of underutilization, while North America represents the remaining 15%. Within EMEA, the construction and infrastructure sectors are experiencing the highest underutilization rates. Government infrastructure projects are facing delays due to funding constraints and regulatory hurdles, leading to reduced demand for our products. We are currently reviewing the terms of our LTAs with customers in the EMEA region, specifically those in the construction sector, to explore potential amendments or alternative solutions. This may involve temporarily reducing minimum volume commitments or offering alternative product mixes to better align with their current needs. To address the rising underutilization charges, we are implementing the following strategies: strengthening communication with our customers to gain a better understanding of their challenges and proactively identify potential underutilization risks. This includes regular meetings with key account managers and the implementation of an early warning system to flag potential volume shortfalls. Where contractually permissible, we are exploring options for flexible volume adjustments to accommodate short-term fluctuations in demand. This may involve allowing customers to defer a portion of their committed volume to future periods or offering alternative product options. We are intensifying our sales and marketing efforts to identify new customers and expand our market share in regions where demand remains strong. This includes targeting new industries and exploring opportunities in emerging markets. Our legal team is conducting a thorough review of all LTA contracts to ensure that we are enforcing the terms and conditions effectively. This includes evaluating our options for pursuing legal remedies in cases of persistent underutilization. We are investing in data analytics tools to better track LTA performance and identify patterns of underutilization. This will enable us to make more informed decisions and proactively address potential issues. Specifically, we are developing a dashboard that provides real-time visibility into LTA volume consumption and alerts us to deviations from agreed-upon targets.

I’ll now hand it over to Susan Davis to walk you through the financials.

Susan Davis, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, John, and hello, everyone.

This quarter’s financial results were underpinned by operational rigor and discipline. Let’s walk through the key metrics.

To start, our Capital Expenditure (CapEx) guidance for the full year has been revised downwards, signaling a shift in investment priorities and operational efficiency. We now project full-year 2023 CapEx to be approximately $2 billion. This represents a significant reduction of $250 million, or approximately 11.1%, compared to the initial guidance of $2.25 billion provided during the Q1 2023 update. This adjustment warrants a closer examination of the factors contributing to this change. We have strategically re-evaluated our ongoing and planned capital projects, identifying opportunities to defer or optimize investments without compromising core growth objectives. A prime example is the postponement of the "Project Phoenix" data center expansion in the EMEA region. While initially budgeted at $80 million for 2023, the project has been pushed to Q1 2024 due to delays in securing necessary permits and revised projections of near-term demand in the region. This decision alone accounts for a significant portion of the CapEx reduction. We have successfully leveraged our scale and negotiating power to secure more favorable terms with key suppliers of equipment and materials. Specifically, we renegotiated contracts for renewable energy infrastructure components, yielding an estimated $30 million in cost savings for 2023. Furthermore, improvements in supply chain management have led to reduced lead times and inventory holding costs, further contributing to CapEx efficiency. A strategic shift towards software-driven automation and process optimization has reduced the need for hardware-intensive investments. For instance, the deployment of a new AI-powered predictive maintenance system across our manufacturing facilities has decreased equipment downtime and extended the lifespan of existing assets, resulting in a reduction in planned equipment replacements. Initial capacity planning models projected a higher demand for certain services, particularly in the cloud computing segment. However, more recent data suggests a slightly slower growth trajectory, allowing us to delay some planned capacity expansions. This is particularly evident in the APAC region, where the construction of a new regional data center has been scaled back, resulting in a $50 million reduction in planned CapEx for 2023. Management has explicitly stated that the CapEx profile is expected to step down sequentially through the second half of the year. This implies a decreasing trend in capital expenditures throughout Q3 and Q4. We anticipate Q3 2023 CapEx to be approximately $550 million. This reflects the continued ramp-down of previously initiated projects and the postponement of certain new investments. It is approximately 15% lower compared to the Q2 CapEx of $650 million. The reduced figure is due to the completion of the North American Logistics Hub upgrade, finalized in July. We anticipate Q4 2023 CapEx to be approximately $450 million. This represents the lowest quarterly CapEx figure for the year, reflecting the culmination of the company's cost-saving initiatives and the completion of several key capital projects. The reduced figure also reflects a seasonal slowdown in infrastructure spending as the year concludes. The revised CapEx guidance reflects a proactive and disciplined approach to capital allocation. While a reduction in CapEx can sometimes signal concerns about growth prospects, in this case, it appears to be driven by a combination of improved operational efficiency, strategic project prioritization, and a refined understanding of market dynamics. The CapEx reduction is expected to have a positive impact on free cash flow (FCF) generation. With lower capital expenditures, the company will have more financial flexibility to pursue other strategic initiatives, such as debt reduction, share repurchases, or potential acquisitions. We estimate that the revised CapEx guidance could increase full-year FCF by approximately 10%. The company's emphasis on project prioritization and optimization suggests a heightened focus on improving ROIC. By carefully evaluating the potential returns of each capital project and allocating resources to those with the highest potential, the company aims to generate greater value for shareholders. While the CapEx reduction is generally viewed positively, there are some potential risks to consider. A significant underinvestment in infrastructure or technology could potentially hinder the company's ability to compete effectively in the long term. Therefore, it is crucial for management to carefully monitor market trends and ensure that capital expenditures remain aligned with the company's strategic growth objectives. During the Q2 earnings call, management emphasized the following points related to CapEx: "We are committed to maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation and ensuring that our investments generate attractive returns." "Our focus on operational efficiency and supply chain optimization has enabled us to reduce our CapEx spending without compromising our growth objectives." "We will continue to monitor market conditions closely and adjust our CapEx plans as needed to ensure that we are making the most effective use of our capital." Q2 saw a 15% increase in revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, reflecting strong growth across several segments, partially driven by investments made in previous periods.

Additionally, our revenue results demonstrated positive momentum. Our second quarter revenue reached $1.845 billion, a result we are pleased to report sits at the high end of our previously issued guidance range of $1.79 billion to $1.85 billion. While this reflects positive sequential growth, we recognize the ongoing challenges reflected in a 7% year-over-year decline from the $1.984 billion reported in Q2 of the previous fiscal year. The sequential increase from Q1's $1.78 billion represents a solid 3.6% growth. This positive momentum was primarily driven by the successful launch of our new "Project Chimera" suite of AI-powered analytics tools. Initial adoption rates exceeded expectations, particularly within the financial services and healthcare sectors. We estimate that "Project Chimera" accounted for approximately $65 million in revenue this quarter, a 30% increase from its Q1 contribution. Following a sluggish Q1, the North American market witnessed a resurgence in demand, fueled by increased capital expenditure among our enterprise clients. We saw a 5% QoQ increase in North American revenue, driven primarily by renewed investment in cloud infrastructure and cybersecurity solutions. Our strategic partnerships with key players in the IoT (Internet of Things) space began to generate tangible revenue. Joint marketing initiatives and integrated product offerings drove a 15% increase in revenue from our IoT-related solutions, contributing approximately $25 million to the overall QoQ growth. Software license renewals tend to peak in Q2. A targeted campaign focused on early renewals with bundled service packages resulted in a higher-than-anticipated renewal rate, contributing an estimated $15 million to the top line. The 7% YoY decline warrants a more in-depth examination. While we achieved sequential growth, several factors contributed to the negative YoY comparison. The ongoing global economic uncertainty, particularly rising interest rates and inflationary pressures, has led to increased scrutiny of IT spending among our clients. Many are delaying or scaling back large-scale projects, impacting our revenue from professional services and consulting. We estimate that macroeconomic factors contributed to a 3% reduction in YoY revenue. The competitive landscape has intensified, particularly in the cloud computing and data analytics segments. New entrants and aggressive pricing strategies from existing competitors are putting pressure on our market share. We are actively addressing this through increased investment in product innovation and enhanced customer service initiatives. As anticipated, revenue from our legacy product lines continued to decline as customers migrate to newer, cloud-based solutions. This decline, while expected, contributed approximately $45 million to the YoY revenue decrease. We are actively managing this transition by offering migration services and incentivizing customers to adopt our modern platforms. The strengthening US dollar relative to other major currencies, particularly the Euro and the Japanese Yen, negatively impacted our reported revenue. We estimate that unfavorable currency exchange rates accounted for approximately 1% of the YoY revenue decline. Several large-scale project implementations in the EMEA (Europe, Middle East, and Africa) region were delayed due to unforeseen regulatory hurdles and supply chain disruptions. This resulted in a temporary slowdown in revenue recognition from these projects, contributing to the YoY decline. We are working closely with our clients to resolve these issues and anticipate a resumption of project activity in the coming quarters. As stated, the Q2 revenue of $1.845 billion landed at the upper end of our previously provided guidance range of $1.79 billion to $1.85 billion. Our initial guidance was based on a conservative outlook, factoring in the aforementioned macroeconomic uncertainties and competitive pressures. However, the stronger-than-anticipated performance of "Project Chimera" and the North American market recovery exceeded our initial expectations. Our initial projections for "Project Chimera" were based on a more gradual adoption rate. However, the positive feedback from early adopters and the compelling value proposition of the AI-powered analytics tools drove stronger-than-expected demand. We had anticipated a more prolonged period of sluggish demand in the North American market. However, a combination of pent-up demand and government stimulus measures fueled a faster-than-expected recovery in capital expenditure among our enterprise clients. Looking ahead to Q3, we anticipate continued sequential growth, albeit at a more moderate pace. We are issuing revenue guidance of $1.87 billion to $1.93 billion. This reflects our expectation of sustained momentum from "Project Chimera," ongoing recovery in the North American market, and the anticipated resumption of delayed projects in EMEA. We anticipate a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven by strong cloud adoption rates. However, we remain mindful of the ongoing macroeconomic uncertainties and competitive pressures, which could impact our performance. We are committed to executing our strategic priorities, including investing in product innovation, strengthening our strategic partnerships, and enhancing our customer service capabilities, to drive sustainable long-term growth. We are also actively exploring opportunities to mitigate the impact of currency exchange rate fluctuations through hedging strategies.

Now I’ll pass it to Michael Lee to provide color on execution.

Michael Lee, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

From a delivery and operations standpoint, this was one of our more efficient quarters in recent memory.

A big part of that was our sales performance by segment, their respective margin levels, and management's commentary. In Q3 2024, our revenue mix continued to evolve, reflecting both market-specific dynamics and the impact of our strategic initiatives. While certain segments faced headwinds, others experienced robust growth, demonstrating the strength of our diversified portfolio. Smart mobile devices generated approximately $840 million in revenue, representing 42% of our total Q3 revenue of $2.0 billion. While this segment remains our largest contributor, its performance reflects the ongoing slowdown in the global smartphone market and intensifying competition. Revenue increased by 13% sequentially, primarily driven by the launch of our new "Apex" processor targeted at mid-range devices and successful promotions during the back-to-school season. However, year-over-year revenue declined by 19%, attributable to weaker demand for premium smartphones and increased market share capture by competitors utilizing more aggressive pricing strategies. Average selling price (ASP) and product mix remained relatively flat year-over-year. This indicates that while we maintained our pricing structure, we weren't able to offset the volume decline through higher-value product sales. We believe this is partially due to the success of our Apex processor, which while boosting volume, has a lower ASP than our flagship solutions. Gross margins in the Smart Mobile Devices segment were 38%, down slightly from 40% in the prior year. This compression is due to the pricing pressure mentioned earlier and increased component costs, particularly for advanced display technologies and memory. John mentioned that "The mobile market is undoubtedly challenging. We are actively addressing this through a multi-pronged approach. First, we are accelerating the development of our next-generation AI-powered mobile platform, targeting a late Q4 launch to regain competitive edge. Second, we are expanding our partnerships with regional smartphone manufacturers in Southeast Asia and Latin America to diversify our customer base and capture growth in emerging markets. Finally, we're optimizing our supply chain to mitigate cost pressures and improve gross margins. We expect the launch of our new Apex Pro SOC with enhanced AI capabilities to drive significant volume in Q1 2025." Home and Industrial IoT contributed approximately $380 million to Q3 revenue, representing 19% of the total. This segment demonstrates consistent and steady growth, reflecting the increasing adoption of connected devices in both consumer and industrial applications. Revenue increased by 4% sequentially and 3% year-over-year. Growth was primarily fueled by demand for our energy management solutions for smart homes and our edge computing platforms for industrial automation. We saw particularly strong growth in the European market, driven by government incentives for energy-efficient home upgrades. Gross margins in the Home and Industrial IoT segment were a healthy 45%, benefiting from our focus on higher-value, differentiated solutions and a favorable product mix. Susan noted that "Our IoT business continues to be a reliable growth engine. We are investing heavily in expanding our product portfolio to address the evolving needs of both the home and industrial markets. This includes developing advanced sensor technologies, secure connectivity solutions, and AI-powered analytics platforms. We are particularly excited about our recent partnership with a major robotics manufacturer to integrate our edge computing platform into their next-generation industrial robots. This will enable real-time data processing and intelligent decision-making at the edge, unlocking significant productivity gains for our customers." The Automotive segment generated approximately $260 million in revenue, accounting for 13% of total revenue. This segment experienced exceptional growth, driven by the increasing demand for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and in-vehicle infotainment (IVI) systems. Revenue increased by a remarkable 36% sequentially and a staggering 199% year-over-year. This growth reflects our successful design wins with leading automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers. Our development of the "DriveCore" platform, a scalable and modular automotive computing platform, has been a key differentiator. Gross margins in the Automotive segment were 48%, the highest among all our segments. This reflects the high value and complexity of our automotive solutions, as well as our strong relationships with key customers. John stated that "Our automotive business is exceeding our expectations. The electrification and autonomous driving trends are creating tremendous opportunities for us. We are committed to investing in R&D to maintain our leadership position in this rapidly evolving market. We are currently working on developing advanced sensor fusion algorithms and AI-powered perception systems to enable safer and more autonomous driving experiences. We anticipate continued strong growth in this segment in the coming years, particularly as more electric vehicles are manufactured." The Communications Infrastructure and Data Center segment contributed approximately $240 million to Q3 revenue, representing 12% of the total. This segment faced significant challenges due to the ongoing inventory correction in the data center market and delays in 5G infrastructure deployments. Revenue declined by 40% sequentially and 38% year-over-year. We believe this downturn is temporary and expect a recovery in the second half of 2025. Gross margins in the Communications Infrastructure and Data Center segment were 35%, reflecting the lower volume and increased pricing pressure. Susan acknowledged that "The current downturn in the communications infrastructure and data center market is disappointing but not unexpected. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate the impact of this slowdown, including reducing operating expenses and reallocating resources to higher-growth areas. We remain confident in the long-term growth prospects of this market, driven by the increasing demand for bandwidth and computing power. We are working closely with our customers to develop next-generation solutions that will enable them to meet the evolving needs of their end-users." The Personal Computing segment generated approximately $60 million in revenue, representing 3% of the total. This segment is highly volatile, reflecting the cyclical nature of the PC market. Revenue increased by 44% sequentially, driven by seasonal demand for back-to-school laptops and desktops. However, year-over-year revenue declined by 45%, reflecting the overall weakness in the PC market. Gross margins in the Personal Computing segment were 30%, the lowest among all our segments. This reflects the commoditized nature of the PC market and intense price competition. John said that "The personal computing market remains challenging. We are focused on selectively participating in this market by offering differentiated solutions for specific niches, such as high-performance gaming laptops and ultra-portable business notebooks. We are also exploring opportunities to leverage our AI expertise to develop innovative solutions that enhance the user experience in personal computing." While challenges persist in specific segments, our diversified portfolio and strategic investments are positioning us for long-term growth. We remain focused on executing our strategy, driving innovation, and delivering value to our shareholders. We expect to see continued growth in the Automotive and IoT sectors, which will help offset the softness in the Smart Mobile Devices and Communications Infrastructure markets. Our Q4 guidance reflects this expectation, with overall revenue projected to be flat to slightly up sequentially.

We also saw execution gains related to wafer sales and the breakdown to wafer quantity and ASP for this quarter. We shipped approximately 573,000 300-millimeter equivalent wafers this quarter. This represents a 9% decrease compared to the 627,000 wafers shipped in the same quarter last year (Q3 2023). While this decline is not ideal, a deeper dive reveals several contributing factors and mitigating circumstances. It's crucial to understand the breakdown by wafer size. While the headline number is in 300mm equivalents, we also ship 200mm and smaller wafers. Our 300mm wafer shipments, which represent the bulk of our revenue, were down approximately 7% year-over-year, accounting for roughly 485,000 units this quarter compared to 522,000 last year. The smaller wafer sizes (200mm and below) experienced a steeper decline of around 15%, falling from 105,000 equivalent units to approximately 88,000. This steeper drop in smaller wafer sizes is primarily attributed to the ongoing industry-wide transition to larger wafer formats and a decrease in demand from legacy applications. Geographically, the distribution of our wafer shipments also provides valuable insight. North American demand remained relatively stable, experiencing a minor decline of only 2%, which can be attributed to a slight slowdown in the data center segment. However, the Asia-Pacific region, excluding China, saw a more significant drop of approximately 12%. This decline is primarily due to inventory correction among our major Taiwanese and South Korean customers in the consumer electronics sector, particularly related to smartphone components. China, on the other hand, showed resilience, with wafer shipments only declining by 5%, reflecting the continued domestic demand for semiconductors in areas like electric vehicles and industrial automation. European sales followed a similar pattern to North America, remaining relatively consistent with a 3% dip, mainly due to the ongoing geopolitical uncertainties impacting manufacturing output. Furthermore, the end-market applications significantly influence our wafer shipment volumes. We observed a decrease in demand from the consumer electronics sector, approximately 15% year-over-year, as mentioned earlier. The PC market's continued weakness also contributed to this decline. However, the automotive sector, particularly electric vehicles (EVs), remained a bright spot, with wafer shipments increasing by 18% year-over-year. The industrial sector experienced a moderate increase of 5%, driven by demand for power management ICs and sensors. The data center sector, though showing initial signs of slowing, is still a significant contributor, accounting for roughly 28% of our total wafer shipments. Strategically, we are actively mitigating the overall volume decline by focusing on higher-value applications and strengthening relationships with key customers in resilient sectors like automotive and industrial. We are also investing in capacity expansion for advanced nodes, particularly 7nm and below, to cater to the growing demand from high-performance computing and AI applications. To this end, we are adding an additional 10,000 wafer starts per month (WSPM) of 5nm capacity at our Fab 3 in Taiwan by Q4 2025. Our ASP declined approximately 1% year-over-year. This is primarily driven by changes in the product mix shipped during the quarter. Specifically, we saw a higher proportion of shipments in less advanced technology nodes (28nm and above), which command lower ASPs compared to our more advanced nodes (14nm and below). The average ASP for our 300mm wafers was approximately $1,250 this quarter, compared to $1,263 in Q3 2023. While seemingly a small decline, it represents a significant impact on our overall revenue. A key driver of this ASP shift is the increased demand for mature node wafers used in power management and analog applications, which often carry lower price tags than the leading-edge digital logic devices. A detailed look at the different technology nodes shows that our 7nm node ASP actually increased by 3% due to strong demand and limited supply. However, this increase was offset by the decline in ASP for our 28nm and 40nm nodes, which experienced a 5% and 7% reduction, respectively, due to increased competition and pricing pressure. The geographic mix also played a role in the ASP decline. Shipments to China, while holding steady in volume, generally have lower ASPs due to local pricing dynamics and the prevalence of mature technology nodes. Conversely, shipments to North America, which traditionally command higher ASPs, saw a slight decline in volume, further contributing to the overall ASP decrease. From a strategic perspective, we are actively working to improve our ASP by focusing on the following initiatives: shifting our focus towards higher-value applications and advanced technology nodes, particularly in the high-performance computing, AI, and automotive sectors. We are also actively managing our capacity allocation to prioritize products with higher margins. We are investing in differentiated technologies and intellectual property (IP) to create value-added solutions that command premium pricing. This includes developing specialized process technologies for power management, RF, and analog applications. We are continuously working to reduce our manufacturing costs through process improvements, yield enhancements, and economies of scale. This will allow us to maintain our margins even in the face of pricing pressure. We are investing in advanced manufacturing equipment and automation to achieve these goals. We are forging strategic partnerships with key customers and technology providers to develop customized solutions that meet their specific needs and command higher ASPs. For example, we are collaborating with a leading AI chip designer to develop a custom 3nm process technology tailored for their next-generation AI accelerators. While the 9% decline in wafer shipments and the 1% decline in ASP are concerning, we believe that these are temporary headwinds. The underlying demand for semiconductors remains strong, driven by the continued growth of the digital economy and the increasing adoption of advanced technologies like AI, 5G, and electric vehicles.
